q1.prompt: You already hold a pointer to a node and must splice it out. Which shape keeps that edit local?

choices.label: Linked list — relink neighbors in O(1)
Array — shift the tail after the hole

wrong_array.prompt: An array turns the local edit into a tail shift.
wrong_array.explanation: Removing index i from an array moves the n-i-1 later values. With the relevant list nodes already in hand, the edit changes neighboring links instead.

q2.prompt: Which workload makes a linked list the wrong default?

choices.label: When the hot path is random index access
Never — lists beat arrays for every access pattern

wrong_refuse.prompt: Index jumps are expensive on lists.
wrong_refuse.explanation: Avoid a linked list when the hot path is random index access. Avoid claiming O(1) access to the k-th element. Avoid mutating next without keeping a reference to the remainder.

success.prompt: You matched lists to local splices and avoided them when index jumps dominate.
